source.title: Diagnostic challenge in a patient with nephropathic juvenile cystinosis: a case report.

confirmation.summary: High free cystine in granulocytes and two CTNS splice-site variants proven by transcript analysis.
evidence: A cystine-binding protein assay showed a high free cystine content in granulocytes
two novel heterozygous single nucleotide substitutions of c.329G > C and c.329 + 2 T > C

note.text: Since he was three, our son's urine tests have kept showing sugar and protein, and nobody could explain why. He grew and developed normally and felt well. Later tests also showed extra amino acids in his urine and a low uric acid level in his blood. At twelve, an eye examination with a special lamp found tiny crystals in the clear front part of his eyes.
note.author: Peter's Kiro, written from the article's findings; not the parent's words
